scripts/run_acceptance_test.py hard-codes the REV02 300-question workbook, so it could not take this bank without editing it. The benchmark instead POSTs each question verbatim to the application's own /api/ask endpoint ({"question": ...}, every control at its default), the stateless path the UI serves; no application file was changed.

Input Tokens = prompt tokens of the one answer-generation call (the chat-templated prompt tokenized in the server process, as reported by the MLX generator). Output Tokens = tokens the MLX worker generated for that call, including text later removed or replaced by validation (4 withheld answers). No other generative call; the evaluator's embedder is not counted. All 100 questions report both counts.

Duration = client-side time.perf_counter() (monotonic) round trip from sending the HTTP request to receiving the complete response, in seconds (3 dp). /api/ask returns after the live evaluation, so Duration includes it (a fraction of a second) and HTTP/serialization overhead. Component times are the server's own timings_ms/server_timings_ms. Questions ran strictly sequentially; one warm-up question was sent first and excluded from every statistic; no other benchmark or test process was running.

0 execution errors, 0 timeouts, 0 retries, 0 skipped; each question asked exactly once. The only failure was the first server start, refused by the app's own memory preflight before any question was sent; it was not worked around (no threshold change) — memory was freed and the server restarted unchanged.

(a) AI-assisted rubric scoring, not SME-signed. (b) 'Generated Answer' is the delivered answer exactly as returned (80 are the standard decline sentence; 4 are withholding notices; 2 are definitions-quoted fallbacks).
